lesson.menu_desc: Negative questions and question tags: wouldn't it make sense to...? / isn't the real risk...? / ..., didn't it? -- persuading people who do not report to you
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 22 -- Influencing Without Authority -- Negative questions and question tags for persuasion
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fabiana Michelly Silva | Lesson 22 -- Influencing Without Authority
lesson.grammar_point: negative questions and question tags for persuasion

listenings.text: Thanks for making time. I don't manage anyone in this room, so I'm not here to tell you what to do. I'm here to ask a question. Penang cost us eleven days, didn't it? Sales felt it first, Finance felt it second, and our clients felt it the whole time. So wouldn't it make sense to stop depending on a single plant for our keyboards? Here is the proposal: a second supplier in Monterrey for one product line, keyboards only, for ninety days. Yes, the unit price is four percent higher. But isn't the real pain point the delay, not the unit price? One lost week costs us more than a full year of that difference. I've already talked to Daniel in Sales Operations, and he has agreed to champion a pilot, provided it starts small. So this is a quick win, not a revolution. We can review it in ninety days, can't we? If the numbers don't work, we walk away. Shouldn't we at least find out?

Hi Fabiana, it's Daniel from Sales Operations. Quick one after the meeting. I have to admit, you won me over, and I think you swayed Finance too. The way you asked questions instead of making demands really worked. Nobody felt pushed, did they? Two things before Thursday. First, Finance wants the ninety-day review to include the freight cost, not just the unit price, so let's add that. Second, the vice president asked me who owns the pilot. I said you do, and that I'm your ally on the sales side. And one piece of advice: the team in Monterrey is new to us, so let's pre-wire the kickoff with their account manager before we announce anything. Anyway, nice work. Let's grab a coffee tomorrow and plan it.

extra_audio.text: Fabiana opens by saying she does not manage anyone in the room, so she is there to ask a question. She reminds everyone that Penang cost them eleven days. She asks whether it would make sense to stop depending on a single plant. She proposes a second supplier for keyboards only, for ninety days. She admits the unit price is higher, but asks whether the real pain point is the delay. Finally, she suggests they review the pilot in ninety days and walk away if the numbers do not work.

items.situation: Finance says a second supplier is too expensive. Point them to the real problem with a question.
tips: Isn't the real pain point the delay, not the unit price?
Negative question: invites agreement instead of starting a fight.

items.situation: You want the team to start small. Suggest it without giving an order.
tips: Wouldn't it make sense to start with one product line?
Wouldn't it make sense to + base verb = a soft suggestion.

items.situation: Remind the room that everyone saw the last delay. Use a tag.
tips: We all saw what happened in Penang, didn't we?
Past positive statement + didn't we? with a falling tone.

items.situation: Someone says the pilot is too risky. Answer with a tag that invites a yes.
tips: We can always walk away after ninety days, can't we?
can + can't we? The tag repeats the auxiliary.

items.situation: Daniel from Sales has not said a word. Bring him in.
tips: Daniel, you felt this first on the sales side, didn't you?
A tag on someone's own experience brings them into the conversation.
